findings.title: Overly Permissive CORS Whitelist with Credentials Reflection Enables Cross-Origin Refresh Token Theft
findings.scenario: An attacker creates a malicious page hosted on Cloudflare Quick Tunnels (*.trycloudflare.com), Pinggy, or a domain starting with env.clientUrl (e.g. https://clientUrl.attacker.com). When an authenticated user visits the attacker's page, a client-side fetch is executed to /api/auth/refresh with header 'x-refresh-token: 1'. Because origin.includes('trycloudflare') evaluates to true, CORS reflects the attacker origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. The refreshCsrfGuard header check passes because custom headers are permitted on whitelisted CORS origins. The backend returns newly rotated accessToken and user details in the JSON response body, which the attacker script reads directly.
findings.impact: Complete account takeover of any logged-in web user who visits an attacker-controlled site or tunnel.
findings.reproduction: Deploy local server; execute fetch('http://localhost:5000/api/auth/refresh', { method: 'POST', credentials: 'include', headers: { 'Origin': 'https://evil.trycloudflare.com', 'x-refresh-token': '1' } }); verify response header Access-Control-Allow-Origin equals attacker origin and credentials allowed.
findings.remediation: Replace substring and prefix matching (.includes, .startsWith) with a strict, exact-match array of allowed origin strings. Never allow wildcard or public tunnel domains in production CORS configuration.
findings.regressionTest: CORS preflight and actual POST requests with Origin 'https://evil.trycloudflare.com' or 'http://localhost.attacker.com' must be rejected with 403 or omitted Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.

findings.title: Missing select: false on passwordHash Field in User Mongoose Schema
findings.evidence: passwordHash: { type: String, required: true },
findings.scenario: In Mongoose, any schema path without select: false is loaded by default in every query (User.find, User.findById, User.findOne, User.findByIdAndUpdate). Although auth.service.js uses .select('+passwordHash') (demonstrating the developer intended for it to be deselected by default), omitting select: false causes passwordHash to be loaded in other services (such as payment.service.js, video.service.js, or admin endpoints) unless manually excluded with .select('-passwordHash'). Any endpoint returning a User object without manual field projection leaks the Argon2id password hash.
findings.impact: Exposure of Argon2id password hashes to unauthorized API consumers, logs, and external adapters, increasing risk of offline dictionary attacks.
findings.reproduction: Execute User.findById(id) in Node console without .select(); inspect the returned document to observe passwordHash present.
findings.remediation: Set select: false on passwordHash in backend/src/models/AUTH/User.js and configure a toJSON schema transform to delete passwordHash upon serialization.
findings.regressionTest: Query User.findOne() without field projections and assert that returned object does not contain property 'passwordHash'.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Account Lockout Denial of Service (DoS) on Targeted Users and Admins
findings.scenario: An unauthenticated attacker sends 5 invalid passwords for a known target email (e.g. admin@macreation.in or student emails). The target user's account is locked for 15 minutes. Continued requests increase lockout duration to 1 hour (10 failures) and 4 hours (15 failures). Because there is no CAPTCHA, no administrative unlock endpoint, and no self-service email unlock mechanism, an attacker running a simple 15-minute cron job can keep administrators and students permanently locked out of the application.
findings.impact: Permanent denial of service for administrative accounts and target student accounts with zero privileges required.
findings.reproduction: Send 5 POST requests to /api/auth/login with valid email and incorrect password; observe 6th request rejected with 423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED.
findings.remediation: Couple lockout with IP-based and email-based rate limits in Redis; present CAPTCHA / Cloudflare Turnstile after 3 failed attempts; implement an email unlock link; exempt admin accounts from automatic lockouts without secondary MFA or administrative reset capabilities.
findings.regressionTest: Verify account lockout cannot be triggered across different IP addresses without triggering CAPTCHA / rate limiting, and verify an unlock endpoint exists.

findings.title: Concurrency Race Condition in Refresh Token Rotation (RTR) Triggers False-Positive Breach Lockout
findings.scenario: When a web page with multiple concurrent data fetches experiences token expiration, multiple simultaneous API calls receive 401 and immediately dispatch concurrent POST /api/auth/refresh requests with the same refresh token. Because findOne and save are non-atomic, the second incoming request observes isRevoked: true and mistakenly classifies the legitimate race as a token replay attack ('POSSIBLE_TOKEN_THEFT_DETECTED'), instantly revoking all active sessions and logging the user out.
findings.impact: Frequent unexpected logouts and session termination for legitimate users during normal multi-tab or concurrent request browsing.
findings.reproduction: Issue two simultaneous asynchronous HTTP POST requests to /api/auth/refresh with identical refresh token cookie; verify that one request fails with 'Token reuse detected' and deletes all sessions.
findings.remediation: Use atomic findOneAndUpdate({ tokenHash, isRevoked: false }, { $set: { isRevoked: true, revokedReason: 'TOKEN_ROTATION', revokedAt: new Date() } }). Implement a 10-30 second grace period where requests presenting the immediate predecessor token receive the newly generated token pair without triggering breach containment.
findings.regressionTest: Send 2 concurrent refresh requests with identical valid refresh token; verify both succeed or the second receives the new token pair without revoking the session.

findings.title: User Enumeration via Differentiated Status Codes and Error Messages
findings.scenario: While the implementation introduces DUMMY_ARGON2_HASH to eliminate timing discrepancies for non-existent users, it returns distinct HTTP status codes (403 ACCOUNT_INACTIVE, 423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED) and distinct error messages for existing accounts. In addition, registerUser returns 409 CONFLICT if an email exists. An attacker can determine whether an arbitrary email address is registered by either attempting registration or triggering 5 failed login attempts to observe a 423 status code.
findings.impact: Account discovery and email address harvesting for targeted phishing and credential stuffing attacks.
findings.reproduction: Send login requests with non-existent email -> returns 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS. Send 5 invalid login requests for existing email -> returns 423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED, confirming existence.
findings.remediation: Return generic error responses for login failures (e.g. 401 Invalid credentials or account unavailable) without leaking active/locked status in public unauthenticated endpoints.
findings.regressionTest: Assert that responses for non-existent emails, locked accounts, and incorrect passwords return identical HTTP 401 status and error structure.

findings.title: CSRF Guard Bypass on Mobile Platform Fallback to HttpOnly Cookie
findings.evidence: const rawRefreshToken = platform === 'WEB' ? req.cookies?.refreshToken : req.body?.refreshToken || req.cookies?.refreshToken
findings.scenario: refreshCsrfGuard explicitly skips validation when x-client-platform is set to MOBILE_IOS or MOBILE_ANDROID under the assumption that mobile clients pass refresh tokens in req.body. However, authController.js line 61 falls back to req.cookies?.refreshToken if req.body.refreshToken is not provided. In contexts where custom headers can be set (such as via permissive CORS or browser webviews), passing x-client-platform: MOBILE_ANDROID completely bypasses the CSRF guard while still using the victim's cookie.
findings.impact: Bypasses the CSRF defense mechanism intended for cookie-authenticated clients.
findings.reproduction: Send POST request to /api/auth/refresh with header 'x-client-platform: MOBILE_ANDROID' without 'x-refresh-token: 1'; verify request is accepted and executes token refresh.
findings.remediation: When platform is not WEB, strictly require req.body.refreshToken and never fall back to req.cookies. Conversely, for WEB, strictly require cookies and enforce SameSite=Strict cookies with an anti-CSRF token.
findings.regressionTest: Verify that POST /api/auth/refresh with x-client-platform: MOBILE_ANDROID and empty body returns 400/401 and ignores cookies.

findings.title: Inability to Logout with Expired Access Token Leaves Refresh Token Active
findings.evidence: router.post('/logout', authenticate, refreshCsrfGuard, asyncHandler(c.logout))
findings.scenario: The /logout endpoint enforces the authenticate middleware, which rejects expired access tokens with 401 'Session expired. Please login again'. If a user's 15-minute access token has expired and they click 'Log Out', the request is rejected before reaching authController.logout. As a result, the RefreshToken record in MongoDB remains active (isRevoked: false) and the HttpOnly cookie is not cleared from the browser.
findings.impact: Stale sessions and valid refresh tokens remain in the database and user browser after attempted logout.
findings.reproduction: Wait 15 minutes for access token expiration (or forge an expired JWT); issue POST /api/auth/logout with expired token; verify 401 error is returned and refreshToken cookie remains set in browser.
findings.remediation: Allow /logout to proceed even if the access token is expired, or create an unauthenticated logout fallback that extracts and revokes the refresh token cookie and clears the cookie headers.
findings.regressionTest: Send POST /api/auth/logout with an expired access token and valid refresh cookie; verify response is 200 OK and cookie is cleared.

findings.title: In-Memory Login Rate Limiter Lacks Distributed Redis Store and Skips Non-Production
findings.scenario: express-rate-limit uses default in-memory storage without Redis backing. In clustered or multi-container deployments, each process maintains an independent attempt table, multiplying allowed brute-force attempts. Rate limit state is completely wiped on server restarts. In addition, the skip predicate disables rate limiting entirely when NODE_ENV is not explicitly set to 'production', leaving local, staging, and load-test environments exposed to Argon2 CPU exhaustion.
findings.impact: Bypass of login rate limits in clustered environments and total absence of DoS protection in staging/dev deployments.
findings.reproduction: Start multi-core cluster; dispatch 10 login requests across processes; observe each worker tracking counters independently.
findings.remediation: Connect express-rate-limit to Redis using rate-limit-redis. Scope the skip option strictly to automated test runners rather than entire non-production environments.
findings.regressionTest: Verify that rate limit counters are shared across multiple instances via Redis keys.

findings.title: Inconsistent JWT Secret Configuration and Hardcoded Fallback String
findings.evidence: const jwtSecret = process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'your-default-jwt-secret-key-change-it'
findings.scenario: AuthService uses a hardcoded fallback string ('your-default-jwt-secret-key-change-it') while the authenticate middleware imports env.jwtSecret from config/env.js (which has no fallback). In development environments where JWT_SECRET is omitted, AuthService signs tokens successfully with the default string, but authenticate throws a 500/401 error because secret is undefined. If the fallback string is ever deployed, tokens can be forged trivially.
findings.impact: Insecure default secret risk and configuration divergence between token issuance and token verification.
findings.reproduction: Unset JWT_SECRET in environment; run AuthService.issueTokens() and then pass the resulting token to authenticate middleware; observe verification failure.
findings.remediation: Use env.jwtSecret from config/env.js uniformly in AuthService. Enforce non-empty high-entropy JWT_SECRET during server startup in all environments.
findings.regressionTest: Verify AuthService.issueTokens uses env.jwtSecret and throws during application startup if secret is missing or insecure.

findings.title: Single Session Logout Does Not Invalidate Associated Playback Sessions
findings.scenario: While logoutAll and terminatePreviousSessions explicitly execute PlaybackSession.deleteMany({ user: userId }), the standard logout method only deletes the AccessTokenSession and marks the RefreshToken revoked. Any PlaybackSession UUID token issued to that browser for video streaming remains valid and can continue to access HLS video segments until the PlaybackSession expires.
findings.impact: Unrevoked video playback sessions persist after user logout.
findings.reproduction: Generate a PlaybackSession token; invoke /api/auth/logout; verify the playback session token remains functional on /api/videos streaming routes.
findings.remediation: Add PlaybackSession invalidation for the current session or user inside AuthService.logout().
findings.regressionTest: Call logout() and assert that PlaybackSession records for that session are invalidated.

findings.title: Zero Automated Unit and Integration Test Coverage for Authentication Module
findings.evidence: backend/package.json contains no test script (only k6 load tests); 0 unit or integration test files exist for auth in the repository.
findings.scenario: The application handles critical cryptographic operations (Argon2id hashing, token issuance, refresh token rotation, account lockout, CSRF protection, session revocation) with 0% automated unit or integration test coverage. Any refactoring or dependency update risks introducing silent regressions without detection.
findings.impact: High risk of security and logic regressions across all authentication and authorization flows.
findings.reproduction: Inspect backend/package.json scripts.test; run test suite to verify absence.
findings.remediation: Add a testing harness (Vitest or Jest) with comprehensive integration test suites for all 7 auth endpoints and middleware.
findings.regressionTest: Execute npm test and verify minimum 90% branch and statement coverage across auth routes, controllers, and services.

findings.title: Unauthenticated / Unchecked AES-128 Key Delivery Endpoint Lacks Playback Token Validation
findings.evidence: router.get('/:videoId/key', requireVideoEntitlement, asyncHandler(c.getVideoKey)) calls VideoService.getVideoKey({ video, userId, req }), which verifies User.playbackLocked and WatchLog watch limit, but completely ignores req.query.token and does not verify the existence of an active, valid PlaybackSession.
findings.impact: Any entitled user possessing a standard Bearer JWT can retrieve the raw 16-byte AES-128 DRM key directly without starting a playback session, allowing offline caching and decryption.
findings.reproduction: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <STUDENT_JWT>' http://localhost:5000/api/videos/<VIDEO_ID>/key -> Returns 200 OK with raw 16-byte binary decryption key without initiating PlaybackSession.
findings.remediation: Validate req.query.token against PlaybackSession in VideoService.getVideoKey, verify session.expiresAt > new Date(), session.video == videoId, and session.user == userId before returning key buffer.
findings.regressionTest: Call GET /api/videos/:videoId/key without a valid, unexpired playback session token and assert response is 401/403.

findings.title: Automatic Reactivation of Deactivated Videos in requireVideoEntitlement Middleware
findings.evidence: let video = await Video.findOne({ _id: req.params.videoId, active: true }); if (!video) { video = await Video.findOneAndUpdate({ _id: req.params.videoId, status: 'READY' }, { $set: { active: true } }, { new: true }); }
findings.impact: When an administrator deliberately sets video.active = false, any incoming user request touching requireVideoEntitlement automatically updates the database to active: true, overriding administrative intent.
findings.reproduction: Set video.active = false via admin CMS. Perform GET /api/videos/:videoId/hls/manifest.m3u8 as an entitled user. Database record for video is silently flipped back to active = true.
findings.remediation: Remove the auto-heal write mutation from authorization middleware; return AppError('Video not found', 404, 'NOT_FOUND') if video is inactive.
findings.regressionTest: Query an inactive video with status 'READY' through requireVideoEntitlement and verify that it returns 404 and does not modify active: false in DB.

findings.title: HLS Segment Streaming Endpoint Omits Watch Limit and Quota Verification
findings.evidence: router.get('/:videoId/hls/:segment', requireVideoEntitlement, asyncHandler(c.getHlsSegment)) only executes requireVideoEntitlement, which checks plan ownership. Neither getHlsSegment nor requireVideoEntitlement checks WatchLog.totalWatchedSeconds >= maxAllowedSeconds.
findings.impact: Users whose watch limit has expired can continue streaming all video chunks (.ts) directly from MinIO as long as they retain the encryption key, bypassing all plan watch caps.
findings.reproduction: Consume full watch quota for a video. Issue GET /api/videos/:videoId/hls/res_1080p_seg_000.ts. Server returns 200 OK with video/MP2T content.
findings.remediation: Add watch quota verification middleware to getHlsSegment or validate active non-expired PlaybackSession on segment streaming requests.
findings.regressionTest: Request HLS segment after WatchLog.totalWatchedSeconds exceeds maxAllowedSeconds and verify 403 WATCH_LIMIT_REACHED is returned.

findings.title: HLS Variant Sub-Playlists and Multi-Bitrate ABR Segments Omit Playback Session Token
findings.evidence: getHlsManifest replaces /(segment_\d+\.ts)/g with token query parameter, but TranscodeService outputs ABR segments named res_%v_seg_%03d.ts and sub-playlists res_%v.m3u8. Sub-playlists are piped raw from MinIO without token rewriting in getHlsSegment.
findings.impact: Mobile players (Android/iOS) fail with 401 Unauthorized when requesting variant playlists or segments because token query parameters are omitted and players do not transmit custom Bearer headers.
findings.reproduction: Request GET /api/videos/:videoId/hls/manifest.m3u8?token=<UUID>. Sub-playlist links inside master.m3u8 lack token parameters.
findings.remediation: Update regex to match res_\w+\.m3u8 and res_\w+_seg_\d+\.ts, and perform token injection in getHlsSegment when serving variant .m3u8 playlists.
findings.regressionTest: Request master playlist with token and verify that all sub-playlist URLs and subsequent segment URLs carry the token query parameter.

findings.title: Trivial Bypass and Insecure Substring Matching in Key Delivery Hotlinking Protection
findings.evidence: const origin = req.headers.origin || req.headers.referer || ''; const isAllowed = origin.startsWith(env.clientUrl) || origin.includes('localhost') || origin.includes('pinggy') || origin.includes('trycloudflare'); if (origin && !isAllowed) ...
findings.impact: Requests omitting Origin/Referer (e.g. curl, scrapers, mobile clients) evaluate origin to empty string and bypass checks. Furthermore, origin.includes('localhost') allows domains like attacker-localhost.com.
findings.reproduction: Send GET /api/videos/:videoId/key with Header 'Origin: http://evil-localhost.com' or without Origin/Referer headers; request passes hotlink guard.
findings.remediation: Parse origin with URL parser, remove localhost/tunnel substrings from production logic, and enforce strict origin matching against env.clientUrl.
findings.regressionTest: Send key requests with spoofed origins (e.g. http://localhost.attacker.com) and verify rejection with 403 UNAUTHORIZED_DOMAIN.

findings.title: Unvalidated watch-event Route Allows Arbitrary Watch Seconds and Quota Corruption
findings.evidence: router.post('/:videoId/watch-event', asyncHandler(c.reportWatchEvent)) does not attach validate(watchEventSchema). In VideoService.reportWatchEvent, watchedSeconds = Math.max(0, Math.floor(Number(seconds) || 0)) has no upper bound constraint for type === 'started'.
findings.impact: Clients can submit seconds: 1e9 to exhaust user watch quota in one request, or seconds: Infinity to inject NaN into MongoDB $inc, permanently disabling watch limit enforcement.
findings.reproduction: POST /api/videos/:videoId/watch-event with body { token, type: 'started', seconds: 100000000 }. WatchLog.totalWatchedSeconds increases by 100,000,000.
findings.remediation: Attach validate(watchEventSchema) to watch-event route, and clamp seconds to 0 in type === 'started'.
findings.regressionTest: Submit watch-event with seconds: 99999 and assert validation rejects request with 400 Bad Request.

findings.title: Concurrency Race Condition in reportWatchEvent Allows Double-Counting of Watch History
findings.evidence: if (!session.consumed) { session.consumed = true; await session.save(); ... WatchLog.findOneAndUpdate(...) } uses in-memory check without atomic database CAS.
findings.impact: Concurrent requests with the same session token both observe consumed === false and execute WatchLog increment and history push multiple times.
findings.reproduction: Send 5 concurrent POST requests with type: 'started' using the same token. Multiple requests pass the condition and push duplicate history records.
findings.remediation: Execute atomic update: PlaybackSession.findOneAndUpdate({ _id: session._id, consumed: false }, { $set: { consumed: true } }) and proceed only if a document was modified.
findings.regressionTest: Dispatch 5 parallel 'started' watch-events with the same token and assert only 1 succeeds in recording history.

findings.title: Missing Magic Byte Verification on Raw Video Uploads
findings.evidence: uploadRawVideo only checks path.extname(filename) and mimeType string from client headers. Unlike uploadBookFiles, it does not inspect file magic bytes.
findings.impact: Arbitrary non-video payloads with spoofed MIME types and .mp4 extensions are written to NVMe storage and submitted to ffprobe/ffmpeg child processes.
findings.reproduction: Upload text file renamed to sample.mp4 with Content-Type: video/mp4. File is accepted, stored in /tmp/uploads/, and queued to BullMQ.
findings.remediation: Inspect stream chunk prefix for ISO BMFF / Matroska signatures (ftyp for MP4/MOV, 0x1A45DFA3 for WebM/MKV) before streaming to disk.
findings.regressionTest: Upload an executable renamed to .mp4 and verify middleware rejects it with 415 Unsupported Media Type.

findings.title: Unhandled WriteStream Error in Busboy Video Upload Causes Server Process Crash
findings.evidence: writeStream = fs.createWriteStream(rawFilePath); fileStream.pipe(writeStream); does not attach writeStream.on('error', ...). On disk full (ENOSPC), Node.js crashes with an unhandled stream error.
findings.impact: Uploading files when disk is near full crashes the Node.js API process, causing total service denial.
findings.reproduction: Simulate write error / full filesystem during uploadRawVideo. Unhandled error event on writeStream terminates Node process.
findings.remediation: Attach writeStream.on('error', (err) => { cleanup(err.message); next(new AppError('File write error', 500, 'IO_ERROR')); }).
findings.regressionTest: Emit error on writeStream and verify API responds with 500 without process termination.

findings.title: Premature Temporary Directory Deletion Prevents BullMQ Transcoding Retries
findings.evidence: processTranscodeJob has a finally block executing fs.rmSync(uploadDir, { recursive: true, force: true }). If step 5 (upload to MinIO) fails on attempt 1, uploadDir is deleted, causing BullMQ attempts 2 and 3 to immediately fail with file not found.
findings.impact: Transient worker failures (MinIO timeout, Redis hiccup) cannot be recovered by BullMQ retry mechanisms.
findings.reproduction: Simulate network error during MinIO upload. Attempt 1 deletes uploadDir in finally. BullMQ retries and fails with 'Raw video file not found'.
findings.remediation: Only delete uploadDir in finally if job succeeded or if job.attemptsMade >= job.opts.attempts.
findings.regressionTest: Fail attempt 1 of transcode job and verify rawFilePath remains intact for attempt 2.

findings.title: FFmpeg ABR Pipeline Fails on Videos Without Audio Tracks or Non-H.264 Codecs
findings.evidence: Stream copy (-c:v:0 copy) breaks on VP9/ProRes because MPEG-TS container does not support VP9. Furthermore, -var_stream_map explicitly maps a:0, a:1, a:2, which crashes FFmpeg on silent videos without audio.
findings.impact: Silent screen captures and WebM/MKV uploads fail transcoding completely.
findings.reproduction: Upload silent MP4 with no audio stream. FFmpeg exits with code 1: 'Stream map a:0 matches no streams'.
findings.remediation: Inspect probeMetadata output; if no audio stream exists, omit audio maps from -var_stream_map. Re-encode stream 0 if codec is not h264.
findings.regressionTest: Transcode a silent video and verify TranscodeService completes successfully.

findings.title: Encryption Key and Storage Path Discrepancy Between HlsService and TranscodeService
findings.evidence: TranscodeService saves a random 16-byte key to video.encryptionKeyHex in MongoDB, while HlsService uses deterministic HMAC and does not set encryptionKeyHex. Re-transcoding with HlsService leaves the old encryptionKeyHex in DB while files are encrypted with the HMAC key.
findings.impact: Calling POST /:videoId/transcode-hls on an existing video breaks client playback permanently due to key mismatch.
findings.reproduction: Upload video via TranscodeService (writes encryptionKeyHex). Call POST /api/videos/:id/transcode-hls. Key returned by getVideoKey no longer decrypts stream.
findings.remediation: Align HlsService to use TranscodeService's key generation and storage logic, or retire HlsService in favor of TranscodeService.
findings.regressionTest: Re-transcode video via HlsService and assert served decryption key matches media segments.

findings.title: HTTP Headers Already Sent Exception in Realtime SSE Connection Limiter
findings.evidence: publicController.events flushes SSE headers and writes ': connected\n\n' before calling addRealtimeClient(res). Inside addRealtimeClient, if clients.size >= MAX_SSE_CLIENTS, it attempts res.status(429).json(...), triggering ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT.
findings.impact: Server throws unhandled ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT exceptions when SSE capacity is reached.
findings.reproduction: Open 100 SSE connections, then open connection 101. Express crashes with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT.
findings.remediation: Check clients.size before setting headers and writing data in publicController.events.

findings.title: TOCTOU Concurrency Race Condition in Order Creation Leading to Duplicate Charging and Double Spend
findings.evidence: createOrder queries: Payment.findOne({ plan: plan._id, status: 'paid', user: userId }). It checks only for 'paid', ignoring existing pending ('created') orders. receipt is generated as `mac_${Date.now()}`, which bypasses Razorpay DUPLICATE_ORDER deduplication. No distributed lock or unique DB index exists.
findings.scenario: A student double-clicks 'Buy Now' or submits concurrent automated order creation requests. Both requests find no 'paid' record, generate distinct `mac_${Date.now()}` receipts, and create two distinct Razorpay orders. The student's card/UPI is debited twice for the same plan, creating two separate 'paid' records in MongoDB with duplicate charges.
findings.impact: Direct customer financial loss, dispute and chargeback liabilities, and corrupt payment accounting.
findings.reproduction: Send 2 concurrent POST /api/payments/order requests with identical { planId } and Bearer token; both succeed with HTTP 201 and create two active Razorpay orders.
findings.remediation: 1. Check for active 'created' orders within a 30-minute lock window before creating an order. 2. Use deterministic receipt key: `mac_${userId}_${planId}` so Razorpay returns DUPLICATE_ORDER on concurrent calls. 3. Acquire a distributed lock on Redis key `lock:payment:order:${userId}:${planId}`.
findings.regressionTest: Execute 10 concurrent POST /api/payments/order requests for the same user and plan; assert exactly 1 returns 201 and 9 return 409 Conflict.

findings.title: Unhandled Buffer Length Mismatch in Webhook HMAC Verification Causes Uncaught Exception / DoS
findings.evidence: handleWebhook computes `expected` (64-char hex string) and evaluates: if (expected.length !== signature.length || !crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(expected), Buffer.from(signature))). It compares string character length instead of byte length. If an attacker submits a 64-char multi-byte UTF-8 string (e.g. 64 double-byte chars = 128 bytes), the character length check passes, and crypto.timingSafeEqual throws an unhandled RangeError [ERR_CRYPTO_TIMING_SAFE_EQUAL_LENGTH].
findings.scenario: An external attacker sends POST /api/payments/webhook with header `x-razorpay-signature` consisting of 64 two-byte UTF-8 characters. The endpoint crashes with an uncaught RangeError, causing an unhandled 500 error and webhook processing pipeline failure.
findings.impact: Denial of Service on payment webhook handler, unhandled error logging, and service degradation.
findings.reproduction: Send POST /api/payments/webhook with header `x-razorpay-signature: \u00e9...` (64 characters) and body `{}`; observe unhandled RangeError crash.
findings.remediation: Validate signature format with regex `/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/`. Parse both strings into hex buffers: `const expBuf = Buffer.from(expected, 'hex'); const sigBuf = Buffer.from(signature, 'hex'); if (expBuf.length !== sigBuf.length || !crypto.timingSafeEqual(expBuf, sigBuf)) throw new AppError('Invalid webhook signature', 400);`
findings.regressionTest: Submit webhook with 64-char multi-byte UTF-8 signature; assert HTTP 400 Bad Request returned cleanly without throwing RangeError.

findings.title: Complete Absence of Amount and Currency Verification During Payment Verification and Webhook Capture
findings.evidence: verifyPayment only verifies HMAC of `orderId|paymentId` and never calls Razorpay API to confirm captured amount or currency. handleWebhook extracts `entity = req.body?.payload?.payment?.entity` and marks payment 'paid' without verifying `entity.amount === Math.round(payment.amount * 100)` or `entity.currency === payment.currency`.
findings.scenario: If a transaction is partially captured, paid in an unauthorized currency, or if gateway amounts desynchronize, the backend blindly marks the plan as fully paid without verifying that the captured amount matches the required plan price.
findings.impact: Financial leakage, underpayment vulnerabilities, and inability to reconcile financial accounting records.
findings.reproduction: Trace verifyPayment and handleWebhook; note that neither method inspects or compares `amount` or `currency` against `payment.amount`.
findings.remediation: In handleWebhook: verify `entity.amount === Math.round(payment.amount * 100)` and `entity.currency === payment.currency` before setting status 'paid'. In verifyPayment: fetch payment details via `getRazorpayClient().payments.fetch(razorpayPaymentId)` and assert `amount` and `status === 'captured'`.
findings.regressionTest: Send webhook with `entity.amount` differing from `payment.amount * 100`; assert payment status is NOT changed to 'paid' and error is logged.

findings.title: Permanent Lifetime Entitlement Granted Without Subscription/Plan Duration Expiration or Revocation
findings.evidence: Ownership is checked via: Payment.exists({ user: req.user.sub, plan: course.plan, status: 'paid' }). The Payment schema contains no `expiresAt`, `validUntil`, or `isRevoked` fields. Plans with `billing` and `duration` (e.g. 1 month retainer) grant permanent, perpetual access with no expiration or revocation mechanism.
findings.scenario: A customer purchases a 30-day course or 1-month retainer plan. After 30 days, 1 year, or indefinitely, the customer retains full DRM video and course streaming access because Payment.exists always returns true.
findings.impact: Severe revenue leakage, inability to offer recurring subscriptions or time-limited access, and breach of retainer service agreements.
findings.reproduction: Create plan with duration '30 days'. Pay for plan. Simulate 60 days passing; send GET /api/videos/:id/hls; entitlement is still granted.
findings.remediation: Add `expiresAt: Date` and `isRevoked: Boolean` to Payment schema. Populate `expiresAt` upon order completion based on `plan.duration`. Update requireEntitlement to require `{ user: req.user.sub, plan: course.plan, status: 'paid', isRevoked: { $ne: true }, $or: [{ expiresAt: null }, { expiresAt: { $gt: new Date() } }] }`.
findings.regressionTest: Verify access for payment with `expiresAt` set to past timestamp returns HTTP 403 NOT_ENTITLED.

findings.title: Irreversible Failure Lockout via markPaymentFailed Blocks Legitimate Payment Completion
findings.evidence: markPaymentFailed sets `status: 'failed'` for { razorpayOrderId, user: userId, status: 'created' }. verifyPayment queries only `{ status: 'created' }` with fallback `{ status: 'paid' }`. If markPaymentFailed is invoked (e.g. client modal canceled or network timeout) while payment is debited by Razorpay, verifyPayment throws 404 NOT_FOUND and webhook ignore the capture.
findings.scenario: A user's browser closes or triggers the payment failed handler during checkout. Meanwhile, Razorpay charges the customer's account. When the user returns to verify payment or when Razorpay sends `payment.captured`, the database refuses to transition the order from 'failed' to 'paid', leaving the student debited without access.
findings.impact: Customer charged without access, high support overhead, and unrecoverable order state.
findings.reproduction: Call POST /api/payments/failed for an order. Then call POST /api/payments/verify with valid Razorpay payment signature; server returns 404 NOT_FOUND.
findings.remediation: Allow verifyPayment and handleWebhook to transition an order from 'failed' to 'paid' if a cryptographically verified Razorpay signature or webhook confirms successful capture.
findings.regressionTest: Mark order failed, then call verifyPayment with valid HMAC signature; assert order transitions to 'paid' and returns 200 OK.

findings.title: Unhandled Zero-Price (Free) Plan Crash in Razorpay Order Creation
findings.evidence: Plan model permits `price: { type: Number, required: true, min: 0 }`. In createOrder: `amount: Math.round(plan.price * 100)`. When price is 0, amount is 0. Razorpay API rejects orders under 100 paise with BAD_REQUEST_ERROR: amount should be at least 100. createOrder throws uncaught gateway error, crashing with HTTP 500.
findings.scenario: Admin creates a free trial or promotional plan with price 0. Any student attempting to enroll in this plan receives HTTP 500 because Razorpay rejects amount 0.
findings.impact: Inability to offer free courses or trial plans; unhandled 500 internal server errors.
findings.reproduction: Create Plan with price 0. Call POST /api/payments/order; observe Razorpay API error and 500 response.
findings.remediation: In createOrder, check if `plan.price === 0`. If free, immediately create Payment with `status: 'paid'`, `amount: 0`, and return success without invoking Razorpay API.
findings.regressionTest: Call createOrder for plan with price 0; assert 201 Created with instant 'paid' status and no Razorpay order creation.

findings.title: Missing Webhook Payload Audit Trail & Replay Event Deduplication Table
findings.evidence: Payment.js defines `rawWebhook: Object`, but handleWebhook never writes to it or records incoming payloads. Razorpay header `x-razorpay-event-id` is never extracted or checked against a deduplication table, preventing auditability of webhook retries.
findings.scenario: Razorpay retries a webhook or network issues duplicate deliveries. There is no audit record showing what timestamp, headers, or payloads Razorpay transmitted, making financial disputes and reconciliation unresolvable.
findings.impact: Zero forensic traceability for automated financial transactions; inability to debug payment capture issues.
findings.reproduction: Post valid webhook to /api/payments/webhook. Inspect Payment document; rawWebhook is undefined and no WebhookLog exists.
findings.remediation: Persist `rawWebhook: entity` on Payment document and store incoming events in a dedicated WebhookEvent collection with unique index on `eventId`.
findings.regressionTest: Process webhook; assert `rawWebhook` is persisted on the payment document.

findings.title: Missing Unique Constraints on razorpayOrderId and razorpayPaymentId
findings.evidence: In Payment.js: `razorpayOrderId: { type: String, index: true }` and `razorpayPaymentId: { type: String, index: true }`. Neither field defines `unique: true`. Compound entitlement indexes are commented out in the schema file.
findings.scenario: Under race conditions or duplicate webhook replays, multiple Payment documents can store the exact same order ID or payment ID. Queries returning single documents yield non-deterministic results.
findings.impact: Data inconsistency, duplicate payment records, and corrupted payment-to-order mapping.
findings.reproduction: Insert two Payment documents with identical razorpayOrderId; MongoDB accepts both without error.
findings.remediation: Add `unique: true, sparse: true` to razorpayOrderId and razorpayPaymentId. Uncomment and enforce schema compound indexes.
findings.regressionTest: Attempt to insert two Payment records with identical razorpayOrderId; assert MongoDB throws E11000 duplicate key error.

findings.title: Mongoose Validation Failure in createOrder when User Lacks Phone Number
findings.evidence: In Payment.js, `phone: { type: String, required: true, trim: true }`. In createOrder: `const finalPhone = dbUser.phone || phone || ''`. In payment.validator.js: `phone` is optional. If user has no phone in DB and omits it from body, finalPhone is empty string. Mongoose rejects empty string on required path, throwing ValidationError after Razorpay order creation.
findings.scenario: A user without a saved phone initiates checkout without passing a phone in the request. Razorpay creates an order, but Payment.create fails with Mongoose ValidationError. The user receives HTTP 500 and the Razorpay order is orphaned.
findings.impact: Orphaned Razorpay orders and 500 internal server errors during checkout for users without phone numbers.
findings.reproduction: Set user.phone = '' or undefined. Call POST /api/payments/order with { planId } without phone. Observe 500 ValidationError.
findings.remediation: In createOrderSchema, validate that phone is present or default to a fallback placeholder if DB user lacks phone.
findings.regressionTest: Call createOrder with no user phone and no request phone; assert HTTP 400 Bad Request with descriptive message before invoking Razorpay.

findings.title: Unvalidated Foreign Key References Allow Creation of Orphaned Courses and Inaccessible Content
findings.evidence: CourseService.createCourse directly creates Course documents with req.body.category and req.body.plan without verifying Category.exists({ _id: category }) or Plan.exists({ _id: plan }).
findings.scenario: An administrator submits POST /api/admin/lms/courses with an arbitrary 24-character hex string for category or plan (e.g. from a deleted plan or typo). The course is persisted in MongoDB. Because the plan does not exist, no student can ever purchase or unlock the course. Because the category does not exist, course.category is null, causing it to fall into 'uncategorized' or crash frontend views expecting category metadata.
findings.impact: Data corruption, permanently inaccessible course content, broken curriculum hierarchy, and frontend rendering anomalies.
findings.reproduction: As admin, send POST /api/admin/lms/courses with { category: '660000000000000000000001', plan: '660000000000000000000002', title: 'Orphan Course' }. Request returns 201 Created and persists an unlinked course.
findings.remediation: Add existence checks in CourseService.createCourse: const [catExists, planExists] = await Promise.all([Category.exists({ _id: category }), Plan.exists({ _id: plan })]); if (!catExists) throw new AppError('Category not found', 404, 'CATEGORY_NOT_FOUND'); if (!planExists) throw new AppError('Plan not found', 404, 'PLAN_NOT_FOUND');
findings.regressionTest: Call createCourse with non-existent category/plan IDs and assert it throws 404 CATEGORY_NOT_FOUND / PLAN_NOT_FOUND.

findings.title: Non-Atomic Cascading Deletions Without Transaction Cause Partial Data Loss and Storage Desynchronization
findings.evidence: deleteCategory and deleteCourse delete MinIO assets via deleteMinioVideoAssets, then call Video.deleteMany and Course.deleteMany without a MongoDB transaction session. Neither method cleans up BullMQ transcode jobs or /tmp/uploads/${videoId} files.
findings.scenario: An administrator deletes an active course or category. If MinIO asset deletion times out (accumulating thousands of HLS segment keys in memory via listObjects) or throws a network error, MongoDB records remain while video files are partially erased. Furthermore, active transcode jobs in BullMQ are not removed, causing workers to crash when updating non-existent video records. Additionally, students who paid for the associated plan have their paid course content wiped out without warning, confirmation, or audit trail.
findings.impact: Desynchronized storage state (MinIO vs MongoDB), unhandled background worker crashes in BullMQ, and irreversible deletion of student-paid educational material without audit logging.
findings.reproduction: Trigger DELETE /api/admin/lms/courses/:id while a video in that course is actively transcoding. The video is deleted from MongoDB, but the BullMQ job continues running and throws an unhandled error upon transcode completion.
findings.remediation: Wrap multi-collection operations in a MongoDB session transaction (session.startTransaction()). Replicate BullMQ queue cancellation and /tmp/uploads cleanup from deleteVideo into deleteCourse and deleteCategory. Implement soft-deletion (active: false) and verify no active paid entitlements exist before permitting deletion.
findings.regressionTest: Execute deleteCourse on a course with pending BullMQ transcode jobs and assert the queue job is evicted, local temp directories are purged, and DB operations rollback on MinIO failure.

findings.title: Entitlement Middleware Automatically Mutates Deactivated Videos Back to Active on Read Requests
findings.evidence: if (!video) { video = await Video.findOneAndUpdate({ _id: req.params.videoId, status: 'READY' }, { $set: { active: true } }, { new: true }) }
findings.scenario: An administrator intentionally disables or retracts a video by setting active: false (e.g. copyright notice, outdated content, or quality dispute). When an entitled student requests GET /api/videos/:videoId/key or POST /api/videos/:videoId/playback-token, requireVideoEntitlement detects active: false with status: 'READY' and automatically executes findOneAndUpdate({ $set: { active: true } }), overturning the administrator's deliberate deactivation.
findings.impact: Administrative content control is subverted; read-only requests execute unauthorized state mutations on the database.
findings.reproduction: Set active: false on a READY video in MongoDB. As an enrolled student, request GET /api/videos/:videoId/key. The request succeeds and the database document now has active: true.
findings.remediation: Remove the findOneAndUpdate auto-heal logic from requireVideoEntitlement. Video activation should occur strictly within the transcode worker upon pipeline completion or via an explicit administrative update endpoint.
findings.regressionTest: Deactivate a video (active: false, status: 'READY'), issue a student playback request, and verify the endpoint responds with 404 NOT_FOUND and leaves active: false unchanged.

findings.title: Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use Race Condition in Video Title Uniqueness Allows Duplicate Videos
findings.evidence: Video title uniqueness is checked using an application-level findOne regex query without a matching unique compound index on { course: 1, title: 1 } in Video.js.
findings.scenario: Two administrator requests (or double-click submissions) submit the same video metadata simultaneously. Both requests execute the findOne query concurrently before either document is inserted. Both checks pass, resulting in duplicate video entries with identical titles in the course playlist.
findings.impact: Corrupted curriculum playlists, duplicate transcode jobs, and confused student navigation.
findings.reproduction: Send two concurrent POST /api/admin/lms/videos requests with identical course and title. Both return 201 Created and two identical video records are created.
findings.remediation: Add a unique compound index with collation in backend/src/models/LMS/Video.js: schema.index({ course: 1, title: 1 }, { unique: true, collation: { locale: 'en', strength: 2 } }). Catch MongoDB 11000 duplicate key error and return 409 DUPLICATE_TITLE.
findings.regressionTest: Execute concurrent video creation requests with identical titles and verify exactly one succeeds and the other fails with 409 DUPLICATE_TITLE.

findings.title: Complete Absence of Edit/Update Routes in Admin LMS Module Prevents Safe Metadata Modifications
findings.evidence: backend/src/routes/adminLms.js exposes only POST and DELETE handlers for categories, courses, and videos. No PATCH or PUT routes exist.
findings.scenario: If an administrator makes a typo in a course title, wants to update a thumbnail URL, reorder videos, or toggle active status, there is no API route to perform an update. The only available action is deleting the entire entity. Deleting a course permanently destroys all videos from MinIO and MongoDB, erasing student progress.
findings.impact: Severe administrative usability blocker forcing destructive cascading operations for minor metadata edits.
findings.reproduction: Attempt to send PATCH /api/admin/lms/courses/:id. Express returns 404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND.
findings.remediation: Add PATCH /categories/:id, PATCH /courses/:id, and PATCH /videos/:id routes in adminLms.js with proper validation schemas and service update methods.
findings.regressionTest: Send PATCH /api/admin/lms/courses/:id with an updated title and verify the title is updated without deleting child video records.

findings.title: High-Concurrency Compound Indexes Commented Out in Mongoose Schemas Cause Memory Sorts and COLLSCANs

findings.scenario: On new deployments or fresh database instances where ensure-indexes.js was not manually run, Mongoose autoIndex will not create compound indexes for video playlist lookups and entitlement checks. Video.find({ course: courseId, status: 'READY', active: true }).sort({ order: 1, createdAt: 1 }) falls back to in-memory sorting, and Payment.exists({ user, plan, status: 'paid' }) performs sequential scans across all payments of the user.
findings.impact: Severe database CPU spikes and memory exhaustion under concurrent student video streaming and course browsing.
findings.reproduction: Inspect schema definitions in Video.js and Payment.js; run queries against a newly initialized MongoDB container without executing ensure-indexes.js; verify via explain('executionStats') that queries perform in-memory SORT stages.
findings.remediation: Uncomment compound index definitions in backend/src/models/LMS/Video.js and backend/src/models/LMS/Payment.js so they are automatically registered on application bootstrap.

findings.title: Zod Validation and Mongoose Schema Character Length Mismatches Cause Unhandled Mongoose Errors

findings.scenario: An administrator submits a course title with 170 characters. The Zod validator accepts the request, but Mongoose throws a ValidationError at the database layer. While the error handler catches this as MONGO_SCHEMA_ERROR, it breaks API contract consistency.

findings.regressionTest: Send POST /api/admin/lms/courses with a 161-character title and verify Zod returns a 400 validation error before reaching MongoDB.

findings.title: Student Course Dashboard Groups Courses in Map Without Respecting Category Display Order

findings.scenario: Category A has administrative display order 10, and Category B has order 1. If Course 1 under Category A has course order 0 and Course 2 under Category B has course order 1, Course 1 is processed first, inserting Category A into the Map before Category B. The student dashboard displays Category A ahead of Category B, disregarding the admin display order.
findings.impact: Inconsistent, non-deterministic category ordering on the student LMS dashboard.
findings.reproduction: Create Category A with order 10 and Category B with order 1. Create a course in Category A with order 0. Query GET /api/courses/mine; Category A appears before Category B in the response array.
findings.remediation: Sort the final grouped array before returning: return Array.from(grouped.values()).sort((a, b) => (a.category?.order ?? 9999) - (b.category?.order ?? 9999));
findings.regressionTest: Call listUserCourses with multi-category courses and verify categories are sorted strictly ascending by category.order.

findings.title: Missing Route Parameter Validation and Broken Dead Function finalizeVideoUpload

findings.evidence: AdminService methods (updateUser, deleteUser, upsertSetting, deleteLead, createResource, updateResource, deleteResource, deleteCategory, deleteCourse, deleteVideo) execute destructive state mutations with zero audit logging. No AuditLog model, table, or write operation exists.
findings.scenario: A compromised admin account or rogue insider silently promotes test accounts to admin, deletes student accounts, wipes courses, or alters pricing. When discovered, no audit log exists to identify which admin credentials performed the actions, from what IP address, or at what timestamp.
findings.impact: Violates non-repudiation, OWASP ASVS Section 7, and SOC2/ISO 27001 compliance standards. Forensic investigation after a breach or unauthorized data modification is impossible.
findings.reproduction: Perform PATCH /api/admin/users/:id with { role: 'admin' } or DELETE /api/admin/users/:id. Inspect MongoDB; no audit record is created.
findings.remediation: Create an immutable AuditLog collection and service (recording actorAdminId, ip, userAgent, action, targetEntity, targetId, before, after, timestamp) and invoke it for all state-mutating admin endpoints.
findings.regressionTest: Execute mutation endpoints and verify an AuditLog record is persisted with matching admin ID, target ID, and action.

findings.title: Unrestricted Privilege Escalation & Peer Admin Account Hijacking in updateUser
findings.evidence: static async updateUser(callerAdminId, targetUserId, data) { ... const { name, email, phone, company, role, interest } = data; const user = await User.findByIdAndUpdate(targetUserId, { $set: { name, email, phone, company, role, interest } }, { new: true, runValidators: true })
findings.scenario: Any user with 'admin' role can arbitrarily promote any customer to 'admin'. Furthermore, an admin can change the 'email' of any other admin without superadmin approval or password confirmation, enabling trivial account hijacking of peer administrators via password reset flows.
findings.impact: Full horizontal and vertical privilege escalation. Any compromised admin account can take over all other admin accounts and create unlimited new administrators.
findings.reproduction: Admin A calls PATCH /api/admin/users/<adminB_id> with { 'email': 'attacker@example.com' }. Admin B's email is overwritten with no verification.
findings.remediation: Enforce a distinct 'superadmin' role for role management. Prohibit modifying peer admin credentials or email addresses via generic profile update. Require re-authentication / MFA for privilege modifications.
findings.regressionTest: Attempt role escalation or email change on an admin account from a non-superadmin session; assert 403 Forbidden.

findings.title: TOCTOU Race Condition in Last-Admin Protection Permitting Permanent Administrative Lockout
findings.evidence:
In updateUser: if (data.role === 'customer') { const adminCount = await User.countDocuments({ role: 'admin' }); if (adminCount <= 1) throw new AppError('Cannot demote the last admin', 400, 'LAST_ADMIN') }
In deleteUser: if (targetUser.role === 'admin') { const adminCount = await User.countDocuments({ role: 'admin' }); if (adminCount <= 1) throw new AppError('Cannot delete the last admin', 400, 'LAST_ADMIN') }
findings.scenario: When exactly 2 admins exist, if Admin A demotes Admin B while Admin B demotes Admin A concurrently, both requests execute countDocuments simultaneously, both see count 2, and both proceed to demote the users. The system is left with zero administrators.
findings.impact: Complete administrative lockout from the application with no admins remaining to manage users, content, or system settings.
findings.reproduction: Issue concurrent PATCH /api/admin/users/:id demoting both admins simultaneously. Both requests succeed, leaving 0 admins in database.
findings.remediation: Wrap the admin count check and demotion/deletion inside a MongoDB multi-document transaction with isolation, or use an atomic conditional query with optimistic concurrency control.
findings.regressionTest: Simulate simultaneous demotions using Promise.all; verify that at least one request fails with LAST_ADMIN and exactly one admin remains.

findings.title: Inconsistent Strike Management, Lack of Strike Reset, and Premature Playback Unlocking
findings.evidence: approveIncidentAndUnlockPlayback sets playbackLocked: false on User, but recordingStrikes is never decremented or reset. Furthermore, if a user has multiple pending incidents, approving one incident unlocks playback while other incidents remain pending_review. Also, neither approve nor ban validates incident.status !== 'pending_review', allowing state overwrites.
findings.scenario: A student receives false positive screen capture flags, accumulating recording strikes. Admin approves the incident, but strikes remain incremented forever. Additionally, an admin resolving an already banned incident unlocks playback for a banned account.
findings.impact: Students can be permanently penalized by false-positive strikes with no administrative mechanism to clear them. Multiple incident handling leads to race conditions bypassing security review.
findings.reproduction: Create user with 2 pending incidents. Call POST /api/admin/security-incidents/:id/resolve on incident 1. Observe User.playbackLocked becomes false while incident 2 is still pending_review. Observe recordingStrikes counter is not decremented.
findings.remediation: 1) Check for remaining pending_review incidents before clearing playbackLocked. 2) Provide explicit strike decrement/reset options. 3) Validate state transitions (incident.status === 'pending_review' required). 4) Add direct student strike management endpoint.
findings.regressionTest: Attempt to resolve an incident with status 'user_banned'; assert rejection with 400 INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION. Verify playback is not unlocked if other pending incidents exist.

findings.title: Missing Pagination and Unbounded Database Queries on Admin and LMS Endpoints
findings.evidence: CourseService.listCategoriesAdmin, listCoursesAdmin, and listVideosAdmin call Model.find().sort() with zero limit or pagination. AdminService listUsers, listLeads, and listPayments use hardcoded limit(500) with no page or offset query parameters.
findings.scenario: As LMS video, course, and user tables scale into thousands of records, admin dashboard listing triggers unindexed full collection scans and pulls entire datasets into Node.js heap memory, resulting in high event-loop blocking and Out-of-Memory (OOM) crashes.
findings.impact: Denial of Service (OOM crash) of the Node.js API process. Inability for administrators to view records beyond the first 500 in core admin views.
findings.reproduction: Populate database with 2,000 video records. Request GET /api/admin/lms/videos. All 2,000 records are fetched and serialized in a single query.
findings.remediation: Introduce standardized cursor or offset pagination (page, limit, skip) with reasonable default (e.g. 20) and maximum allowable limit (e.g. 100) across all admin listing endpoints.
findings.regressionTest: Call GET /api/admin/lms/videos?page=1&limit=20; assert response contains paginated items and totalCount metadata.

findings.title: Missing Input Schema Validation on Generic CMS Resources and Route ObjectIDs
findings.evidence: POST /resources/:resource and PATCH /resources/:resource/:id have no body validation schemas. None of the :id route parameters in admin.js are validated against objectIdParamSchema. PUT /settings/:key validates value with z.any(), allowing arbitrary unconstrained payloads.
findings.scenario: Admin or compromised session submits invalid types or corrupted payloads to CMS resources (e.g. invalid plan prices or malformed partner URLs). The unvalidated settings are immediately broadcast to all connected clients via SSE.
findings.impact: Database inconsistency, Mongoose CastError exceptions, and frontend application crashes due to unexpected data shapes broadcast via realtime CMS updates.
findings.reproduction: Submit POST /api/admin/resources/plans with {} or non-schema fields, or PUT /api/admin/settings/brand with { value: null }. The requests bypass Zod validation.
findings.remediation: Define resource-specific Zod schemas for services, plans, pages, faqs, and partners. Apply validate(objectIdParamSchema, 'params') across all :id parameters.
findings.regressionTest: Send invalid body to POST /api/admin/resources/plans; assert 400 ZOD_VALIDATION_ERROR.

findings.title: Unsafe Object Property Access and Potential Crash in Generic Resource Model Lookup
findings.evidence:
const models = { services: Service, plans: Plan, pages: Page, faqs: FAQ, partners: Partner }
static getModel(resource) { const Model = models[resource]; if (!Model) throw new AppError('Unknown resource', 404, 'NOT_FOUND'); return Model; }
findings.scenario: If an incoming request provides resource='constructor' or 'toString', models[resource] resolves to the native Object constructor or method instead of undefined. Calling Model.find() on Object causes a TypeError: Model.find is not a function, crashing the request into a 500 error.
findings.impact: Unhandled 500 Internal Server Error when probing prototype properties on the generic resources API endpoint.
findings.reproduction: Send GET /api/admin/resources/constructor. Observe 500 Internal Server Error with TypeError: Model.find is not a function.
findings.remediation: Use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(models, resource) or Map or Object.create(null) for resource lookup.
findings.regressionTest: Send GET /api/admin/resources/constructor; assert 404 NOT_FOUND.

findings.title: Incomplete User Deletion Leaving Orphaned Sessions, Tokens, and Broken Foreign References
findings.evidence: deleteUser calls User.findByIdAndDelete(targetUserId) without deleting or revoking AccessTokenSession, RefreshToken, PlaybackSession, or handling foreign key references in Payment, WatchLog, or SecurityIncident.
findings.scenario: A deleted user leaves orphaned tokens and payment records. When an admin views /api/admin/payments, payment.user is null, triggering frontend null-dereference errors when accessing payment.user.name or email.
findings.impact: Orphaned authentication sessions in database and frontend UI crashes on payment/incident lists due to unhandled null user references.
findings.reproduction: Create user with payment, delete user via DELETE /api/admin/users/:id, query GET /api/admin/payments. Response contains payment with user: null.
findings.remediation: Implement soft delete (isActive: false, isDeleted: true) or explicitly cascade revoke AccessTokenSession, RefreshToken, and null-safe handle/anonymize referencing documents.
findings.regressionTest: Delete a user; verify all associated AccessTokenSession and RefreshToken records are deleted.

findings.title: Missing Update (PUT/PATCH) Routes for LMS Categories, Courses, and Videos
findings.evidence: adminLms.js registers POST and DELETE routes for categories, courses, and videos, but omits PATCH /categories/:id, PATCH /courses/:id, and PATCH /videos/:id. CourseController and CourseService have no update methods for these entities.
findings.scenario: An administrator needs to fix a typo in a video or course title, update thumbnail URL, or adjust category ordering. Because no update endpoints exist, the admin must delete and recreate the entity, destroying student watch progress and historical logs.
findings.impact: Administrative workflow deficiency and data loss risk when making simple metadata modifications.
findings.reproduction: Send PATCH /api/admin/lms/courses/:id. Server returns 404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND.
findings.remediation: Implement updateCategory, updateCourse, and updateVideo in routes, controllers, and services with corresponding validation schemas.

findings.title: Unhandled ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT Server Exception in SSE Endpoint When Connection Limit Is Exceeded
findings.evidence: events() in publicController.js sets res.status(200), flushes headers, and writes ': connected\n\n' BEFORE invoking addRealtimeClient(res). When clients.size >= MAX_SSE_CLIENTS (100), addRealtimeClient attempts res.status(429).json({ success: false, message: 'Too many connections' }), triggering an unhandled 'Error [ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT]: Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client'.
findings.scenario: Under normal web traffic when 100 clients are connected to SSE, user 101 connecting triggers an uncaught ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT exception. Client reconnection loops exacerbate the issue, repeatedly throwing unhandled exceptions in the Node HTTP server pipeline.
findings.impact: Server instability, error logging spikes, Sentry alert flooding, broken client connection state, and complete failure to communicate rate limiting to overflowing clients.
findings.reproduction: Simulate 100 concurrent SSE connections to /api/public/events. On the 101st request, observe the Node.js server throw ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT when attempting to set status 429.
findings.remediation: Check capacity (clients.size >= MAX_SSE_CLIENTS) in events() BEFORE setting HTTP 200 headers. If at capacity, immediately return res.status(429).json(...) before stream headers are written. In routes/public.js, wrap events in asyncHandler, and in middleware/error.js ensure res.headersSent is checked before attempting error serialization.
findings.regressionTest: Mock clients.size = 100 and issue a GET request to /api/public/events. Assert response status is 429 and no ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT exception is thrown.

findings.title: Complete Denial of Realtime Updates via Global Rate Limit Bypass and Uncapped Per-IP SSE Connections
findings.evidence: In backend/src/app.js, express-rate-limit explicitly skips /api/public/events via skip: (req) => ... req.path === '/api/public/events'. There is no per-IP connection limit, no IP-based rate limiting on /api/public/events, and no authentication required.
findings.scenario: An unauthenticated remote attacker or misconfigured client opens 100 parallel EventSource connections from a single IP. All 100 connections are accepted and occupy every slot up to MAX_SSE_CLIENTS = 100.
findings.impact: Total denial of service for the realtime update subsystem. Every other user across the entire platform is blocked from receiving live CMS updates, and any new visitor triggers the ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT exception.
findings.reproduction: Script 100 concurrent GET requests from a single client IP to /api/public/events. All 100 are accepted without rate limiting, holding all server SSE slots.
findings.remediation: Implement per-IP connection limits (e.g., maximum 3-5 concurrent SSE connections per client IP) and apply a dedicated rate limiter (e.g., max 10 connection attempts per 5 minutes) on /api/public/events.
findings.regressionTest: Attempt 6 concurrent SSE connections from a single IP address. Assert that connections exceeding the per-IP threshold are rejected with HTTP 429.

findings.title: Socket and File Descriptor Leak Due to Missing res.end() on SSE Lifetime Expiration
findings.evidence: In realtime.js, const cleanup = () => { clearInterval(heartbeat); clearTimeout(lifetime); clients.delete(res); }. When the 1-hour MAX_SSE_LIFETIME_MS timeout triggers, cleanup() removes the client from clients and clears timers, but never calls res.end() or destroys the socket.
findings.scenario: When long-running clients remain connected past 1 hour, heartbeats cease, but the underlying TCP connection and Node response stream remain open indefinitely in memory.
findings.impact: Gradual socket, memory, and file descriptor leakage on the server, eventually degrading OS network resources.
findings.reproduction: Temporarily set MAX_SSE_LIFETIME_MS to 1000ms. Open an SSE connection. After 1s, verify client is removed from clients set, but the TCP socket remains in ESTABLISHED state without FIN packet being sent.
findings.remediation: In cleanup(), explicitly call if (!res.writableEnded) { res.end(); } to terminate the HTTP response stream when lifetime expires.
findings.regressionTest: Trigger the lifetime expiration timer and assert that res.writableEnded becomes true and socket terminates.

findings.title: Unrestricted Public Exposure and Gated Bypass of Draft, Internal, and Bespoke Enterprise Plans
findings.evidence: Plan.js schema defines only active: { type: Boolean, default: true } without isPublic, published, or isDraft. CatalogService.getActivePlans() queries Plan.find({ active: true }). PaymentService.createOrder allows purchase of any Plan.findOne({ _id: planId, active: true }).
findings.scenario: An admin creates a custom corporate plan, draft pricing experiment, or internal test tier. Because it defaults to active: true, it immediately appears in the public /api/catalog/plans feed and becomes purchasable by any authenticated user via /api/payments/order.
findings.impact: Business and pricing logic leakage, unintended public purchase of internal or negotiated enterprise contracts, and inability to stage plans in draft mode.
findings.reproduction: Insert a plan with custom negotiated rates for a specific client. Query GET /api/catalog/plans; verify the custom negotiated plan is returned in the public catalog.
findings.remediation: Add isPublic: { type: Boolean, default: true } and isDraft: { type: Boolean, default: false } to Plan.js. Filter by { active: true, isPublic: true, isDraft: false } in CatalogService.getActivePlans(), and validate entitlement eligibility in PaymentService.
findings.regressionTest: Create a plan with active: true, isPublic: false. Query GET /api/catalog/plans and assert the plan is omitted.

findings.title: High-Concurrency Database Bottleneck: Missing Compound Indexes on All CMS Collections (COLLSCAN)
findings.evidence: Queries executed on public routes: Service.find({ active: true }).sort({ category: 1, price: 1 }), Plan.find({ active: true }).sort({ category: 1, price: 1 }), FAQ.find({ active: true }).sort({ order: 1, createdAt: 1 }), Partner.find({ active: true }).sort({ order: 1, createdAt: 1 }). None of these collections define compound indexes matching their filter and sort keys. ensure-indexes.js omitted CMS collections entirely.
findings.scenario: High-traffic bursts on the public homepage or pricing page cause simultaneous unindexed collection scans and memory sort operations across all CMS collections.
findings.impact: Elevated MongoDB CPU usage, slow response times, and degraded throughput under public traffic spikes.
findings.reproduction: Run explain('executionStats') on Service.find({ active: true }).sort({ category: 1, price: 1 }). Verify executionStages.stage is COLLSCAN followed by in-memory SORT.
findings.remediation: Add schema indexes: Service.index({ active: 1, category: 1, price: 1 }), Plan.index({ active: 1, category: 1, price: 1 }), FAQ.index({ active: 1, order: 1, createdAt: 1 }), Partner.index({ active: 1, order: 1, createdAt: 1 }). Update ensure-indexes.js.
findings.regressionTest: Execute explain('executionStats') and assert query plan utilizes IXSCAN with 0 documents examined outside the index.

findings.title: Internal MongoDB ObjectIds and Administrative Activity Broadcast to Anonymous Public SSE Listeners
findings.evidence: broadcastCmsUpdate broadcasts key: String(item._id) along with resource and action ('created', 'updated', 'deleted') to all connected public /api/public/events clients. This occurs even when draft resources or unpublished pages are created or modified.
findings.scenario: An anonymous observer maintains an open EventSource connection to /api/public/events and records real-time notifications revealing internal database ObjectIds, admin creation timing, and unpublished resource identifiers.
findings.impact: Reconnaissance information disclosure; leaks database internal identifiers and operational patterns to unauthenticated users.
findings.reproduction: Listen to /api/public/events with curl. Create a page in admin. Observe the received SSE payload contains the raw MongoDB ObjectId.
findings.remediation: Sanitize the broadcast payload to emit only resource category invalidation signals (e.g. { resource: 'plans', action: 'updated', timestamp: '...' }) without leaking internal MongoDB ObjectIds.
findings.regressionTest: Trigger broadcastCmsUpdate({ resource: 'pages', key: '507f1f77bcf86cd799439011' }). Assert message payload does not expose raw database IDs to public consumers.

findings.title: Missing HTTP Cache-Control and In-Memory/Redis Caching on Public CMS and Catalog Endpoints
findings.evidence: Compare bookController.js:13 (Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600...) with catalogController.js and publicController.js: zero caching headers (Cache-Control, ETag, Last-Modified) are sent on /api/catalog/services, /api/catalog/plans, /api/public/faqs, /api/public/partners, /api/public/settings/:key, or /api/public/pages/:slug. Furthermore, no in-memory or Redis caching layer is implemented despite having Redis and realtime event invalidations.
findings.scenario: Every request from every client or CDN edge results in a fresh database query for static content that rarely changes.
findings.impact: Unnecessary database load and higher TTFB for landing page visitors.
findings.reproduction: Request GET /api/catalog/plans. Check response headers; observe absence of Cache-Control and ETag.
findings.remediation: Add Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600 on public catalog and CMS endpoints, or cache serialized results in Redis invalidated via broadcastCmsUpdate.
findings.regressionTest: Send GET request to /api/catalog/plans. Assert Cache-Control header is present with public cache directives.

findings.title: Missing Input Validation Schemas and Unbounded Queries on Public CMS Route Parameters
findings.evidence: There are no validator files (catalog.validator.js and public.validator.js do not exist). req.params.slug in /api/public/pages/:slug has no format or length validation, and queries in catalog.service.js and public.service.js lack .limit() or pagination.
findings.scenario: Oversized or malformed parameters are passed directly to database queries, and unbounded queries return all records without limit.
findings.impact: Input validation gap; potential query resource consumption if collections grow large.
findings.reproduction: Send GET request to /api/public/pages/ with an oversized 10,000-character parameter string. Request reaches MongoDB query directly without route rejection.
findings.remediation: Implement Zod validator middleware for public routes validating slug format ^[a-z0-9-]+$ (max 100 characters) and add reasonable default limits (e.g. .limit(100)) on collection queries.
findings.regressionTest: Send GET request to /api/public/pages/invalid*slug!. Assert request is rejected with 400 ZOD_VALIDATION_ERROR.

findings.title: Unhandled Unicode Character in Inline Content-Disposition Crashes Server with ERR_INVALID_CHAR
findings.evidence: res.setHeader('Content-Disposition', mode === 'download' ? contentDispositionFilename(book.filename) : `inline; filename="${cleanFilename(book.filename).replace(/"/g, '')}"; filename*=UTF-8''${encodeURIComponent(cleanFilename(book.filename))}`). cleanFilename retains Unicode codepoints > 255. Node.js OutgoingMessage.setHeader throws TypeError [ERR_INVALID_CHAR].
findings.impact: Denial of service for reading any non-ASCII or regional-language PDF books.
findings.reproduction: Create or update a book record with filename 'GeM_मार्गदर्शिका.pdf'. Send GET /api/public/books/<id>/read. The server throws uncaught exception 'ERR_INVALID_CHAR: Invalid character in header content' and fails with 500.
findings.remediation: Sanitize the legacy filename parameter to ASCII-only alphanumeric characters in inline mode (matching contentDispositionFilename fallback: filename.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._ -]/g, '_')), while providing full Unicode in the RFC 5987 filename*=UTF-8'' parameter.
findings.regressionTest: Configure a book with filename 'हिन्दी_गाइड.pdf' and send GET /api/public/books/:id/read. Assert response is HTTP 200 with valid Content-Disposition header.

findings.title: MinIO S3 Storage Leak: Uploaded Objects Orphaned When Controller Metadata Validation Fails
findings.evidence: In uploadBookFiles, Busboy streams the PDF to MinIO before body fields are fully validated. Upon busboy 'finish', req.file is populated and next() is invoked. If BookService.createBook throws AppError('A valid book title is required', 400), completed is already true, and neither the middleware nor controller catches the error to call minioClient.removeObject(VIDEO_BUCKET, fileKey).
findings.impact: Unbounded storage exhaustion in MinIO S3 object storage; financial and operational overhead from orphaned storage pollution.
findings.reproduction: Submit POST /api/admin/books/upload with a valid PDF in 'file' and body.title omitted. API returns 400 BOOK_TITLE_REQUIRED, but file object remains stored in MinIO bucket.
findings.remediation: In uploadBook controller or BookService.createBook, wrap document creation in a try/catch block. If Book.create fails and req.file.fileKey exists, immediately invoke minioClient.removeObject(VIDEO_BUCKET, req.file.fileKey).catch(...) before re-throwing.
findings.regressionTest: Send POST /api/admin/books/upload with missing title. Assert HTTP 400 and verify minioClient.statObject confirms object does not exist in bucket.

findings.title: Unbounded Database Query in Admin Book Listing Lacks Pagination and Limit Controls
findings.evidence: static async listBooks() { return await Book.find().sort({ createdAt: -1 }).populate('uploadedBy', 'name email').lean() }
findings.impact: Memory bloat in Node.js V8 heap, database connection latency spikes, and potential denial-of-service under administrative concurrency.
findings.reproduction: Seed 1,000 book records and call GET /api/admin/books. Observe large payload and excessive memory utilization.
findings.remediation: Introduce pagination query parameters (page, limit with max 100) using .skip((page - 1) * limit).limit(limit) and return { books, total, page, totalPages }.
findings.regressionTest: Call GET /api/admin/books?page=1&limit=10. Assert response returns exactly 10 books and pagination metadata.

findings.title: Information Disclosure: Public Books Endpoint Leaks S3 Object Keys, Backend Storage Type, and Admin User IDs
findings.evidence: getPublicBook executes Book.findOne({ active: true }).sort({ createdAt: -1 }).lean() and spreads the entire Mongoose document into the public JSON response: return { ...book, readUrl: ..., downloadUrl: ... }. This exposes fileKey, storage, fileId, and uploadedBy.
findings.impact: CWE-200 Information Exposure facilitating administrative account enumeration and internal storage layout mapping.
findings.reproduction: Execute unauthenticated GET /api/public/books. Observe fileKey, storage, uploadedBy, and __v present in response body.

findings.title: Socket and Stream Resource Leak on Client Connection Abort During PDF Delivery
findings.evidence: streamBook attaches stream.on('error', ...) and executes stream.pipe(res). When a client abruptly terminates or closes the connection during streaming of large 50MB files, res emits 'close', but stream is neither unpiped nor destroyed.
findings.impact: Socket and memory leaks leading to event-loop lag and connection starvation.
findings.reproduction: Initiate GET /api/public/books/:id/read, read 32KB, and terminate socket connection. Observe MinIO client stream remains un-destroyed.
findings.remediation: Replace stream.pipe(res) with pipeline from 'node:stream/promises' or bind res.on('close', () => { if (!res.writableEnded) stream.destroy(); }).
findings.regressionTest: Simulate client socket closure during streamBook execution and verify stream.destroyed evaluates to true.

findings.title: Unauthenticated and Unthrottled Download Counter Manipulation via HEAD Requests
findings.evidence: In streamBook: if (mode === 'download') { res.on('finish', () => { BookService.incrementDownloads(book._id) }) }. Express routes GET endpoints to HEAD requests automatically, emitting 'finish' without body transmission.
findings.impact: Data integrity violation and artificial skew of business analytics; unnecessary database write load.
findings.reproduction: Send 20 consecutive HTTP HEAD requests to /api/public/books/<id>/download. Query book record and observe downloads count incremented by 20.
findings.remediation: Restrict incrementDownloads to req.method === 'GET' and apply Redis-backed IP rate-limiting or debounce per client IP/session.
findings.regressionTest: Send HEAD request to /api/public/books/:id/download. Verify downloads count does not increment.

findings.title: Broken Admin Preview: Inactive Books Cannot Be Streamed or Verified by Administrators

findings.impact: Defective administrative workflow requiring premature public publication to inspect documents.
findings.reproduction: Upload or patch a book to active: false. Visit /api/public/books/<id>/read. Response is 404 NOT_FOUND.
findings.remediation: Expose authenticated admin routes GET /api/admin/books/:id/read and GET /api/admin/books/:id/download backed by Book.findById(id) without active: true restriction.
findings.regressionTest: Authenticate as admin and request GET /api/admin/books/:id/read on an inactive book. Verify HTTP 200 stream.

findings.title: Missing Compound Database Index on { active: 1, createdAt: -1 } for Public Hero Query

findings.impact: Suboptimal query execution and avoidable database CPU consumption.
findings.reproduction: Run explain('executionStats') on Book.findOne({ active: true }).sort({ createdAt: -1 }). Note SORT operation stage.
findings.remediation: Add schema.index({ active: 1, createdAt: -1 }) and schema.index({ createdAt: -1 }) to Book.js schema.
